transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’m just tired all the time. I mean, I’m a teacher, so I know what normal end-of-the-day tired feels like, but this is different. Even if I sleep through the night, I still feel like I have to really push myself just to get through grading, making dinner, and getting ready for the next morning.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… I have. Most days I can still put on a smile for my students and get through the lessons, but underneath I feel pretty flat. It’s like this gray feeling that follows me home, and even things I usually like, like my garden or painting with watercolors, feel kind of distant.
Do you still enjoy the things you usually like to do?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I still do them sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d say I enjoy them the same way. It’s more like I go through the motions.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite?
I don’t think I’ve noticed much of a change. My appetite seems pretty normal, maybe it varies a little day to day, but nothing that really stands out.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
Not really, no. I mean, some days I feel a little distracted like anyone, but I haven’t noticed a real problem concentrating. I can still keep up with teaching and planning lessons.
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty lately?

Yeah… I guess I have. I keep feeling like I should be handling things better. If my lesson plans take way longer than they should, or I say no to helping mentor a newer teacher, I start telling myself I’m letting people down—my family, the school. It’s not constant, but it’s been there.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve felt down and hard on myself, but I haven’t been thinking that life isn’t worth living.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It’s been about two years now… a little over that, maybe two years and a couple months. It started around when my husband stopped working outside the home and our household routine changed.
During those two years, have you felt this low mood most days?

Yes… most days. I can still put on a smile for my students and get through my lessons, but underneath it’s like this gray, flat feeling. It tends to follow me home, and even things I usually enjoy, like my garden or watercolors, feel kind of far away.
During the past two years, has there been any stretch of two months or longer when you did not feel this depressed?

No, not really. It’s been pretty steady for about two years and two months, since my husband stopped working outside the home and our routine changed. I don’t think I’ve had a full two months where it lifted.
Have you been feeling like you have low self-esteem?

Yes, I think so. I keep telling myself I should be handling things better than I am. Like if my lesson plans take twice as long, or I say no to mentoring a newer teacher, I start thinking I’m letting my family and my school down.
During these past two years, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when your depression became noticeably worse than your usual baseline?
I’m not really sure. It’s been pretty consistently low, so I can’t point to a clear two-week stretch where it got noticeably worse than the usual.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a depressed/flat mood present most days for a little over 2 years, without any remission lasting 2 months or longer, along with low energy/fatigue, reduced enjoyment, and low self-esteem/guilt. There is no clear evidence of a superimposed major depressive episode, and no suicidality, concentration impairment, or appetite change was endorsed. This pattern is most consistent with persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia).
